| [QUESTION-254](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md) v4 | What separates an interpretive organization that constitutes an experiential perspective from one that only processes information, or only represents a perspective, when the separation must not require an episode's current contents to be veridically constrained by their referents, must not be drawn from the verdict it gives on groups and machines, and must justify the queries, interventions and timescales by which it individuates a perspective without appeal to the phenomenal unity it is meant to explain? | The question the exchange of 2026-10-21 ended each pass on. A3: "What differentiates an interpretation that merely processes information from an interpretation that constitutes a perspective?" A5 proposed it for this line. A6 sharpened it to a class of realized organizations "whose identity and unity are invariant under changes in sensory grounding", distinguished from systems "that merely simulate or report the same interpretations". The grounding condition is narrowed here to current veridical grounding, as CLAIM-413 states it, and the question asks for the targets of individuation to be justified too. It narrows [QUESTION-046](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-046.md) to the constitutive thesis, [CLAIM-412](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md). An answer is that thesis's missing sufficiency condition, which [CLAIM-411](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md) presses. | Open |
| [QUESTION-255](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md) v4 | Can an empirical model that genuinely fails to glue, under a specified cover and correspondence between its contexts, take part in one phenomenally unified process, given that a unified experience can contain conflicting interpretations or demands and that such conflicts are not by themselves gluing obstructions? | A7 §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-21, after A6 found a sheaf-theoretic account of global phenomenal unity. The record's self line already reads a coherent self as a global section ([CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md)), and conflict without an overlap as no disunity ([CLAIM-198](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md)). A7 denied that experiential unity is "the existence of one globally consistent assignment of interpretations": "the conflict itself can be a unified experience", and a global assignment "could exist in a merely descriptive model without any corresponding unified process". A review of 2026-10-22 corrected the example: a felt conflict need not be a gluing failure, since one global state can hold both sides. The question is whether a model that genuinely fails to glue, under a cover and correspondence fixed independently, can be part of one unified experience. | Open |
